================= #547 =================
TITLE: feat(source-rest): resumable pagination cursor (persist + seed CursorInBody)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
`CursorInBody` (and cursor pagination generally) exhausts pages **within a run** but never persists the terminal cursor as a resumable bookmark, nor re-seeds it into the next run's first request. For envelope-cursor APIs (Plaid `/transactions/sync`) this forces a full pull every run — correct output, but not incremental.

## Motivation
`tap-plaid`'s `/transactions/sync` advances a `next_cursor` and expects the *saved* cursor to seed the next run. faucet's `replication_key`/`replication_bind` only capture a **record field's** max value; the cursor is an envelope token (`$.next_cursor`), not a record field, so it's uncapturable today.

## Proposed design
```yaml
pagination:
  type: CursorInBody
  next_token_path: "$.next_cursor"
  body_cursor_field: cursor
  persist_cursor: true            # NEW: emit the terminal cursor as StreamPage.bookmark
replication_bind: { source: bookmark, target: body, field: cursor }   # NEW: seed the next run's first request from the saved cursor
```
- Carry the terminal cursor into `StreamPage.bookmark` (rides the existing `StateStore` path — no core trait change).
- On resume, inject the stored bookmark into the first request's body/param before paging.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/rest/src/pagination/mod.rs` (surface the terminal cursor)
- `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (read the stored bookmark, seed the first request)

## Acceptance criteria
- A `CursorInBody` source with `persist_cursor: true` + a state store resumes from the saved cursor (wiremock test: run 1 consumes pages, run 2's first request carries the stored cursor).
- No `faucet-core` trait change; existing cursor configs unaffected.

## Out of scope
- The multi-array (added/modified/removed) fan-out — separate issue.

## References
Found verifying `tap-plaid` for the Meltano→faucet migration. Roadmap: #38


================= #548 =================
TITLE: feat(core,source-rest): multi-array response fan-out to per-stream write modes
LABELS: feature,tier-2

## Summary
A single response envelope that carries **multiple record arrays destined for different write modes** cannot be expressed config-only. `/transactions/sync` returns `added`+`modified` (→ upsert) **and** `removed` (→ delete) from one cursor advance; faucet's one-`records_path`→one-`write_mode`-per-row model can't route them from a single paged response.

## Motivation
`tap-plaid` incremental sync needs added/modified upserted and removed deleted **from the same cursor delta**. Two separate matrix rows would each advance + persist the shared cursor independently and diverge (the delete pass would never see the same delta the upsert pass consumed).

## Proposed design
Let one rest source emit several labeled sub-streams from one response, each routed to a write mode in a single pass:
```yaml
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    tag: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", tag: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  tag: delete }
```
consumed by a sink/topology that maps `tag → write_mode` off the same page (and the same cursor advance).

## Affected crates / files
- `faucet-core` — `StreamPage` gaining tagged sub-batches (or a topology tee that preserves one cursor advance)
- `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` — emit the tagged sub-batches

## Edge cases
- The delete sub-stream must key on the same PK as the upsert stream.
- Ordering: deletes vs upserts within a page must be well-defined.

## Acceptance criteria
- One `/transactions/sync`-style response routes added/modified→upsert and removed→delete in a single run against a keyed sink (integration test).

## Out of scope
- Cursor persistence (separate issue — its prerequisite).

## References
Found verifying `tap-plaid`. Larger change (core + rest). Roadmap: #38


================= #549 =================
TITLE: feat(source-rest): record_ancestors — lift envelope fields onto unwrapped records
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
When `records_path` selects a **nested** array element, there's no way to lift fields from the enclosing **ancestor** (envelope) onto each emitted record. Events-API feeds (Stripe, and any `data.object` webhook/event shape) lose the envelope id/timestamp.

## Motivation
`tap-stripe`'s `subscription_history` keeps every Event and keys on the Event **envelope** `id` (aliased `event_id`). faucet unwraps `records_path: $.data[*].data.object`, emitting the subscription object and discarding the envelope — so `event_id` is unrecoverable by any downstream transform (the field isn't in the record). No data loss under `write_mode: overwrite`, but an upsert-by-key destination has no per-event unique key.

## Proposed design
```yaml
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"
record_ancestors:            # copy named fields from the $.data[*] array-element ancestor onto each record
  event_id: "id"
  event_created: "created"
```
After JSONPath selection, walk each matched leaf's ancestor and copy the named paths onto the record.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/rest/src/extract/` (post-selection ancestor merge)

## Acceptance criteria
- A source with `record_ancestors` lifts the envelope `id`/`created` onto each unwrapped record (unit test over a Stripe-events-shaped body).
- Absent `record_ancestors`, behavior is unchanged.

## Out of scope
- General JOINs across responses (that's `lookup`).

## References
Found verifying `tap-stripe` (`subscription_history.event_id`). Generalizes the Singer events-unwrap+carry-envelope pattern. Roadmap: #38


================= #550 =================
TITLE: feat(source-graphql): offset-into-query-variable pagination (ShopifyQL)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
The GraphQL source only does **top-level cursor** pagination (`pageInfo { hasNextPage, endCursor }` → `after` variable). APIs that page by an **offset embedded inside a query-string variable**, terminating on a short page (not a `pageInfo` boolean), can't be expressed.

## Motivation
`tap-shopify`'s `sessions` and `sales` streams use **ShopifyQL** (`shopifyqlQuery(query: $q)`): the `LIMIT/OFFSET` live inside the `$q` string, results come back columnar (`tableData.rows`), and paging stops when a page returns fewer than `page_size` rows. Neither the graphql cursor paginator nor the rest `Offset` paginator (which writes an offset into a query-param) can drive an offset baked into a nested body variable.

## Proposed design
```yaml
pagination:
  type: Offset
  offset_variable: q_offset          # substituted into the query string / a GraphQL variable
  page_size: 250
  stop_when_short: true              # terminate when a page yields < page_size rows
  template: "... LIMIT 250 OFFSET ${q_offset}"   # or ${q_offset} referenced inside the `variables`
```
Reuse the offset/short-page logic already in `faucet-source-rest`'s `pagination/`.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/graphql/src/config.rs` + `stream.rs` (offset-into-variable pagination style)

## Acceptance criteria
- A graphql source paginates a ShopifyQL-style query by incrementing an offset variable and stops on a short page (wiremock test, 2 pages).

## Out of scope
- Zipping the columnar `tableData.rows` into objects — separate issue (workaroundable via the `sql`/`wasm` transform today).

## References
Found verifying `tap-shopify` (sessions/sales via ShopifyQL). Roadmap: #38


================= #551 =================
TITLE: feat(transform): zip_columns — columnar rows → one object per row
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3

## Summary
A `zip_columns` transform: turn a columnar payload (`{ columns: [{name}], rows: [[v0,v1,…]] }`) into one object per row keyed by column name. Common for analytics/report APIs that return positional arrays.

## Motivation
`tap-shopify` ShopifyQL (`sessions`, `sales`) returns `tableData.rows` (positional arrays) that must be zipped against `tableData.columns[].name`. Expressible today via the `sql`/`wasm` transform, but a small declarative transform is cleaner and reusable (also fits other analytics feeds).

## Proposed design
```yaml
transforms:
  - type: zip_columns
    config: { columns_path: "columns[*].name", rows_path: "rows" }   # → [{col0: v0, col1: v1}, …]
```
A page-level (1→N) transform. Pure; no I/O.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/core/src/stage.rs` (or a `transform-zip-columns` feature) + `cli/src/transforms.rs` wiring + `faucet schema transform`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A columnar page becomes one object per row keyed by column name (unit test); mismatched row width errors clearly.

## Out of scope
- The ShopifyQL offset pagination that produces the columnar pages — separate issue.

## References
Found verifying `tap-shopify` (ShopifyQL columnar results). Workaroundable via `sql` today. Roadmap: #38


================= #552 =================
TITLE: fix(executor,core): child fan-out into write_mode:overwrite is last-writer-wins (silent data loss)
LABELS: bug,tier-1

## Summary
A matrix **child stream fanned out over parent records into a `write_mode: overwrite` sink silently keeps only the LAST parent's rows** — every prior parent's data is truncated. This is silent downstream data loss on a green run (the worst bug class per CLAUDE.md).

## Root cause (verified in code)
- `Pipeline::run` performs `begin_overwrite()` → … → `commit_overwrite()` **within a single run** (`crates/core/src/pipeline.rs:537` / `:602`) — overwrite truncates+swaps per run.
- The CLI executor runs **one `Pipeline::run` per parent record** for a child matrix row (`cli/src/executor.rs` — "one pipeline invocation runs per parent record").
- Therefore child-invocation for parent A truncates+loads A's children; the invocation for parent B truncates (wiping A) + loads B's; … → the destination ends with only the last parent's children.

## Impact (broad)
Any multi-parent child stream written with `overwrite` is affected. Found across the Meltano-tap migration in: **deel** (gp_legal_entity_reports, gp_gross_to_net), **campfire** (budget_accounts, subscriptions), **dualentry** (9 sub-resource streams), **deskera** (account_subgroups), **bamboohr** (per-employee), **navan** (per-type), **ramp** (balance_history), and any `matrix: {parent: …}` → overwrite pattern (isolved/paylocity/lever/adp/ukg_pro/netsuite-lines are correct only when the parent set has one member). Single-parent cases happen to work, which is why it hides.

## Proposed design
Make overwrite fan-out atomic across the whole fan-out group, not per parent-invocation. Options:
1. **Truncate-once + append-all + commit-once**: the executor opens the overwrite staging table once for a child *group*, each per-parent invocation appends into staging, and a single commit-swap runs after the last parent — i.e. lift the overwrite lifecycle from per-`Pipeline::run` to per-fan-out-group.
2. **Single-invocation multi-parent enumeration**: one child run iterates all parent records internally (source-level fan-out) so it's one `Pipeline::run` = one overwrite.

Option 1 is the general fix. Crates: `cli/src/executor.rs` (own the group overwrite lifecycle) + `faucet-core` (`write_mode.rs` / `Pipeline::run` — expose begin/commit so the executor can drive them across invocations, or a `overwrite_group` handle).

## Acceptance criteria
- A child stream fanned out over ≥2 parent records into `write_mode: overwrite` retains ALL parents' rows (integration test with 2 parents → both parents' children present).
- A mid-run failure leaves the prior destination intact (atomic swap only after the whole group succeeds).
- Single-parent behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope
- Per-parent *separate* destination tables (already works via `${parent.*}` in `table_id`).

## References
Found during the Meltano→faucet migration 200%-verification pass (deel/campfire/dualentry/deskera/bamboohr/navan/ramp). Roadmap: #38


================= #553 =================
TITLE: feat(source-rest): offset/limit-in-body pagination (POST-query APIs)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
REST source can't paginate by an **offset/limit carried in the JSON request body** (with an optional body-side incremental filter). Distinct from `CursorInBody` (a token) and `Offset` (a query-param).

## Motivation
`tap-attio` POST-query streams send `{limit, offset}` (and a `created_at $gte` filter) in the JSON body and stop on a short page. Today the template truncates at the first 500 rows. Also relevant to other POST-search APIs.

## Proposed design
```yaml
pagination: { type: OffsetInBody, offset_field: offset, limit_field: limit, limit: 500, stop_when_short: true }
replication_bind: { into: body, name: created_at, template: "{\"$gte\": \"${bookmark}\"}" }
```
Mirror the existing `Offset` logic but write offset/limit into the request body. Crate: `crates/source/rest/src/pagination/` + `stream.rs`.

## Acceptance
A POST source paginates by incrementing a body offset and stops on a short page (wiremock, 2 pages). Roadmap: #38


================= #554 =================
TITLE: feat(source-rest): record-field-max cursor pagination (keyset)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
REST source can't paginate by an offset derived from the **max value of a record field** seen so far (keyset-style), terminating on a short page.

## Motivation
`tap-xero` `journals`/`journals_payments_only` page via `offset = max(JournalNumber)` of the last page (100/page). `Cursor` reads a body/header token and `Offset` uses a numeric page offset — neither computes `max()` of a returned field. Template currently uses `pagination: None` → only the first 100 journals load.

## Proposed design
```yaml
pagination: { type: RecordFieldCursor, field: JournalNumber, into: query, param: offset, agg: max, stop_when_short: true, page_size: 100 }
```
After each page, compute max(field) over the page and inject it as the next request's offset. Crate: `crates/source/rest/src/pagination/`.

## Acceptance
Source walks pages using max(field) and stops on a short page (wiremock). Roadmap: #38


================= #555 =================
TITLE: feat(core): explode with parent-field carry-down
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
`explode` (1→N over an array) **drops the parent record's fields** — there's no option to carry named parent keys onto each exploded child row.

## Motivation
- `tap-bamboohr`: map-envelope `{employees:{<id>:{rows:[...]}}}` explodes `rows[]` while carrying the parent `employeeId` onto each row.
- `tap-hibob`: bulk-history streams explode `results[].values[]` carrying parent `employeeId`.
Today the exploded rows lose the parent id → unjoinable.

## Proposed design
```yaml
- type: explode
  config: { path: rows, carry: { employee_id: "$.id" } }   # copy named parent fields onto each child
```
Crate: `faucet-core` `stage.rs` (Explode).

## Acceptance
Exploding an array copies the named parent field(s) onto each emitted row (unit test). Roadmap: #38


================= #556 =================
TITLE: feat(auth): oauth2_refresh scope + rotated-refresh-token persistence
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
The `oauth2_refresh` provider (a) doesn't send a `scope` on the refresh grant, and (b) doesn't persist a **rotated** refresh token — so providers that rotate the refresh token on every use fail on the second run.

## Motivation
- `tap-onedrive`: Microsoft rotates the refresh token each use + expects `scope=…/.default offline_access` on the grant.
- `tap-rippling`: OAuth token POST uses HTTP Basic + form body and rotates the refresh token; the rotated token must be persisted for the next run.
Strict-scope tenants fail without `scope`; rotation without persistence fails on run 2.

## Proposed design
Add `scope` to the refresh grant, and persist the rotated `refresh_token` via the state store (a durable token store keyed by provider name). Crate: `faucet-auth` (`oauth2.rs` refresh provider) + a small state-backed token cache.

## Acceptance
A refresh grant sends `scope`; a rotated refresh token is persisted and reused on the next run (test). Roadmap: #38


================= #557 =================
TITLE: feat(source-rest): async_job result-set locator/continuation paging
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2

## Summary
`async_job` fetches a **single** result body — it can't follow a **result-set continuation/locator** across multiple result pages.

## Motivation
`tap-salesforce` Bulk API returns results in pages via the `Sforce-Locator` response header (`nextRecordsUrl`-style); a large object's results span several fetches. Today `async_job` grabs one body → large objects truncate. (Note: salesforce's dynamic `instance_url`→base_url is NOT a gap — use the `flow` provider's `base_url_from`, like bullhorn.)

## Proposed design
```yaml
async_job:
  fetch: { url_from: "$.result.url", locator_header: "Sforce-Locator", locator_param: "locator", records_path: "$.records[*]" }
```
Loop the fetch while the locator header/body field is present. Crate: `crates/source/rest/src/async_job.rs` + `stream.rs`.

## Acceptance
An async fetch follows a locator across ≥2 result pages (wiremock). Roadmap: #38


================= #558 =================
TITLE: feat(transform): lookup reference rows from a live API endpoint
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3

## Summary
`lookup` can only read a reference table from **inline values or a local JSONL/CSV file** — it can't resolve labels from a **live API endpoint**.

## Motivation
`tap-hibob` resolves id→name for department / employment_type / title / work_change_type by fetching `/v1/company/named-lists` at runtime and joining. faucet `lookup` has no way to source the reference rows from an HTTP call → those label columns can't be materialized.

## Proposed design
Allow `lookup`'s reference source to be a small REST fetch (URL + auth ref + records_path), fetched once and cached for the run. Crate: `faucet-core`/`faucet-transform` `lookup` + a fetch shim.

## Acceptance
A `lookup` populated from a live endpoint joins id→label over the page (test). Roadmap: #38

### #549 — record_ancestors: lift envelope fields onto unwrapped records
When `records_path` selects a NESTED array element, allow copying fields from the enclosing ancestor onto each emitted record:
```yaml
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"

```
After JSONPath selection, for each matched leaf walk up to the `$.data[*]` array-element ancestor and copy the named paths onto the record. Absent `record_ancestors` ⇒ unchanged. Unit-test over a Stripe-events-shaped body (`{data:[{id, created, data:{object:{...}}}]}`).

### #547 — resumable cursor (persist + seed CursorInBody)
Add `persist_cursor: bool` (default false) to cursor pagination so the terminal cursor rides `StreamPage.bookmark` (existing StateStore path — NO core trait change). On resume, seed the stored bookmark into the first request's body/param before paging. Support a `replication_bind`-style seed of the saved cursor into the first request body field. wiremock test: run 1 consumes pages; run 2's first request carries the stored cursor (drive resume via `Source::apply_start_bookmark`).

### #553 — OffsetInBody pagination (POST-query APIs)
A new pagination style that writes offset+limit into the JSON request BODY (distinct from `CursorInBody` (a token) and `Offset` (a query-param)):
```yaml
pagination: { type: OffsetInBody, offset_field: offset, limit_field: limit, limit: 500, stop_when_short: true }
```
Mirror the existing `Offset` advance logic but write offset/limit into the request body; stop on a short page. wiremock 2-page test asserting the 2nd request body carries the incremented offset.

### #554 — RecordFieldCursor pagination (keyset / max-of-field)
Paginate by the max value of a record field seen so far:
```yaml
pagination: { type: RecordFieldCursor, field: JournalNumber, into: query, param: offset, agg: max, stop_when_short: true, page_size: 100 }
```
After each page compute max(field) over the page and inject it as the next request's offset (into query param or body per `into`). Stop on a short page. wiremock 2-page test.

### #557 — async_job locator/continuation paging
`async_job` currently fetches a single result body. Add result-set continuation:
```yaml
async_job: { fetch: { url_from: "$.result.url", locator_header: "Sforce-Locator", locator_param: "locator", records_path: "$.records[*]" } }
```
Loop the fetch while the locator header (or a body field) is present, appending records across pages; stop when absent/"null". wiremock test following a locator across ≥2 result pages. Keep the existing single-fetch path working when no locator is configured.

### #548 — records_multi: multi-array fan-out in one pass, op-stamped
Let one response emit several record arrays in ONE page (sharing one pagination advance), each stamped with a configurable op-marker field so a downstream `write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` routes them:
```yaml
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  op: delete }

**Body & keyset pagination.** Two styles page without a query param or a response token:

```yaml
# OffsetInBody — POST-query APIs that carry offset/limit in the JSON body.
pagination: { type: OffsetInBody, offset_field: offset, limit_field: limit, limit: 500, stop_when_short: true }

# RecordFieldCursor — keyset: page by the running max (or min) of a record field.
pagination: { type: RecordFieldCursor, field: JournalNumber, into: query, param: offset, agg: max, page_size: 100, stop_when_short: true }
```

Both stop on a short page (fewer than `limit`/`page_size` records) and guard against a non-advancing cursor.

**Resumable cursor (`persist_cursor`).** With `persist_cursor: true`, a `Cursor` / `CursorInBody` stream emits its terminal cursor as the run's `StreamPage` bookmark (persisted via a `state:` store) and, on the next run, seeds that saved cursor into the first request — so an envelope-cursor feed (e.g. Plaid `/transactions/sync`) resumes incrementally instead of re-pulling from the start.

### Multi-array fan-out (`records_multi`) & envelope carry (`record_ancestors`)

```yaml
# records_multi — emit several arrays from ONE response (one pagination advance),
# each stamped with an op marker for a downstream upsert sink's delete_marker.
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  op: delete }
op_field: _op          # each record gets { _op: "<op>" }; default "_op"

# record_ancestors — lift fields from the enclosing array-element ancestor onto
# each record when records_path selects a NESTED array (e.g. Stripe events).
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"
record_ancestors: { event_id: id, event_created: created }
```

`records_multi` is mutually exclusive with `records_path` / `record_ancestors` and requires a JSON response. Pair it with a sink `write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker: { field: _op, values: [delete] }` to route inserts/updates and deletes from a single sync response.

#### Result-set continuation (`fetch.locator_*`)

When a job's results span several pages behind a continuation locator (e.g. the Salesforce Bulk API's `Sforce-Locator` response header), loop the fetch until the locator is absent:

```yaml
async_job:
  # …submit / poll / status…
  fetch:
    url: "/jobs/${job_id}/result"
    locator_header: "Sforce-Locator"   # or locator_body: "$.nextLocator"
    locator_param: "locator"           # sent as ?locator=<value> on each continuation
    records_path: "$.records[*]"
```

Records are appended across pages; the loop stops when the locator header/body is missing, empty, or `"null"`.

content.text: Good call — RabbitMQ is a real gap. Looking at your Streaming & Queues lineup (Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, SQS, NATS), RabbitMQ is the most conspicuous omission: it's the dominant AMQP broker in enterprise/microservices stacks, and it fits faucet cleanly as **both** a source (consume queues, ack after sink-confirm for at-least-once) and a sink (publish to exchanges with routing keys). Definitely worth filing. Let me write it up and file it (then I'll resume the schema work):

input.content:
## Summary

Add a **RabbitMQ (AMQP 0.9.1) source and sink** connector pair — `faucet-source-rabbitmq` / `faucet-sink-rabbitmq` — with a shared `faucet-common-rabbitmq` crate. RabbitMQ is the one conspicuous gap in the "Streaming & Queues" lineup (Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, SQS, NATS are all present) and is the most widely deployed AMQP broker in enterprise / microservices stacks, so it is a frequently-hit integration endpoint for a data-movement toolkit.

## Motivation

Ties to the [Primary Goal](#) (be the fastest, most reliable way to move data between endpoints in Rust) and to Third-Party Connector Friendliness (a broad, credible connector catalog). RabbitMQ is a first-class message broker that many teams use as their integration backbone; faucet already covers every other mainstream queue/stream (Kafka/Kinesis/Pub/Sub/SQS/NATS) but not RabbitMQ. It is a common CDC/event fan-out target *and* a common ingestion source (work queues, topic exchanges, dead-letter exchanges), so both directions are warranted.

## Proposed design

Follow the established queue-connector conventions (mirror `faucet-source-nats` / `faucet-sink-nats` and the Kafka pair). Use the pure-Rust **`lapin`** AMQP client (Tokio-native, no C bindings — keeps the connector cross-compilable for the prebuilt-binary targets).

New crates (all `version = "1.0.0"`, `faucet-core` the only required dep):

- **`faucet-common-rabbitmq`** (`crates/common/rabbitmq/`) — shared connection/auth/TLS config + a `lapin::Connection` builder. Types: `RabbitMqConnection { url | { host, port, vhost, username, password }, tls: RabbitMqTls, connection_name }`, `RabbitMqTls { disable | require | verify_ca | verify_full }`, plus a value-format enum (`json` / `string` / `bytes`) shared with the Kafka/Kinesis common crates' shape.
- **`faucet-source-rabbitmq`** (`crates/source/rabbitmq/`) — consume from a queue. Config: `queue`, optional `bindings: [{ exchange, routing_key }]` (declare + bind), `prefetch` (QoS window, default 100), `ack_mode: on_sink_confirm | auto`, `value_format`, `include_metadata` (routing key / exchange / headers / delivery-tag onto the record), termination `idle_timeout_secs` / `max_messages` (at least one required, mirroring the Kafka/Kinesis sources so a one-shot `run` drains and exits). Implements `Source::stream_pages` natively (pull a QoS-bounded batch per page). **At-least-once:** with `ack_mode: on_sink_confirm`, defer the AMQP `basic_ack` until the pipeline has written+flushed the page (ack the batch's delivery tags on the page bookmark) — the same shape as the Kafka source committing offsets at durable page boundaries.
- **`faucet-sink-rabbitmq`** (`crates/sink/rabbitmq/`) — publish records. Config: `exchange` (default `""` = the default exchange), `routing_key` (static) **or** `routing_key_field` / `routing_key_jsonpath` (per-record), `value_format`, `persistent` (delivery mode 2, default true), `mandatory` (return-on-unroutable), optional `confirm` (publisher confirms — wait for broker acks per batch, the reliable default), `batch_size`. Uses publisher confirms + `FuturesUnordered` for throughput, mirroring the Kafka sink.

Feature flags: `source-rabbitmq` / `sink-rabbitmq` in the umbrella + CLI, `rabbitmq-tls` for TLS (pulls `lapin`'s native-tls/rustls). Add to the `source` / `sink` aggregates and to `full`.

## Affected crates / files

- New: `crates/common/rabbitmq/`, `crates/source/rabbitmq/`, `crates/sink/rabbitmq/` (each with the standard `lib.rs` / `config.rs` / `stream.rs`|`sink.rs` layout + `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]`, per-crate `keywords`, `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`).
- `faucet-stream/Cargo.toml` + `cli/Cargo.toml` — `source-rabbitmq` / `sink-rabbitmq` features, wired into `source` / `sink` / `full`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add both to the `feature-check` matrix.
- `connectors/registry.json` — add verified entries (the `registry_index` test panics otherwise).
- Docs-sync surfaces: root README connector table + counts, `docs/book/src/reference/connectors.md` (capability matrix — streaming/resumable/exactly-once/write-mode columns), `reference/choosing.md`, a `cli/examples/rabbitmq_*` example, `examples/README.md` (+ `examples/docker-compose.yml` with a `rabbitmq:3-management` service for local integration), the crate table in `.claude/rules/architecture.md`.

## Edge cases & failure modes

- **Unroutable publishes** — with `mandatory: true`, a return must surface as an error (DLQ-routable via `write_batch_partial`), not silently vanish.
- **Redelivery on crash** — deferring the ack until sink-confirm means a crash mid-page redelivers the un-acked batch (at-least-once). Document that duplicates are possible and pair with a keyed-upsert sink for effectively-once.
- **Queue vs exchange declaration** — declaring a queue/exchange that already exists with different properties fails (`PRECONDITION_FAILED`); surface it clearly rather than looping.
- **`prefetch` vs termination** — an idle consumer must still honor `idle_timeout_secs` (no busy-wait); a `max_messages` cap must not leave un-acked deliveries.
- **Connection recovery** — a dropped connection mid-stream should reconnect (bounded) and resume from un-acked deliveries, or fail loudly if unrecoverable.
- **Large messages / value formats** — `bytes`/`string`/`json` decoding must handle non-UTF-8 (`bytes` → base64) without panicking.

## Acceptance criteria

- Source consumes a queue and emits records, deferring acks until the pipeline confirms the page (at-least-once), with idle/max-messages termination — verified by a `testcontainers` `rabbitmq:3-management` integration test.
- Sink publishes to the default exchange and to a named exchange with a per-record routing key, with publisher confirms — verified by an integration test that round-trips through the source.
- Both honor TLS config and the shared value formats; config structs derive `JsonSchema`; `faucet list` / `faucet schema source rabbitmq` reflect them.
- ≥90% patch coverage (pure config/decode logic unit-tested; I/O paths covered by the testcontainers tests).

## Out of scope

- AMQP 1.0 (a different protocol; `lapin` is 0.9.1) — file separately if ever needed.
- RabbitMQ Streams (the Kafka-like log) — a distinct protocol/client; separate issue.
- Exchange-to-exchange bindings and advanced topology management beyond declare+bind.

## References

Surfaced from the connector-catalog review (RabbitMQ absent from the Streaming & Queues group alongside Kafka/Kinesis/Pub/Sub/SQS/NATS). Mirrors the existing NATS and Kafka connector pairs. Roadmap epic: #38.

## Offset / limit in the body (POST-query APIs)

For POST endpoints that take `offset`/`limit` in the JSON **request body** (not the query string). The offset advances by each page's record count and paging stops on a short page.

```yaml
pagination:
  type: OffsetInBody
  offset_field: offset
  limit_field: limit
  limit: 500
  stop_when_short: true                # default
```

## Keyset (record-field cursor)

Page by the running **max** (or **min**) of a record field — the pattern APIs like Xero's `journals` use (`offset = max(JournalNumber)` of the last page). Stops on a short page.

```yaml
pagination:
  type: RecordFieldCursor
  field: JournalNumber
  into: query                          # or `body`
  param: offset
  agg: max                             # or `min`
  page_size: 100
  stop_when_short: true
```

## Resumable cursor & multi-array responses

- **`persist_cursor: true`** on a `Cursor` / `CursorInBody` stream saves the terminal cursor as the run's bookmark (via a `state:` store) and seeds it into the next run's first request — so an envelope-cursor feed (e.g. Plaid `/transactions/sync`) resumes incrementally instead of re-pulling from the start.
- **`records_multi`** emits several response arrays in one pass (one pagination advance), each stamped with a configurable `op_field` — pair with a sink `write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` to route added/modified→upsert and removed→delete from a single sync response.
- **`record_ancestors`** lifts fields from an enclosing array-element ancestor onto records unwrapped from a nested `records_path` (e.g. keep a Stripe event's envelope `id` on each unwrapped object).

See the [`faucet-source-rest` README](https://github.com/faucet-hq/faucet-stream/tree/main/crates/source/rest) for the full field reference.

**Collisions** (a prefixed element key would overwrite a sibling) fail loudly with `FaucetError::Transform("explode produced duplicate key 'X'")` — mirroring `flatten` / `keys_case`.

**Carry parent fields down (`carry`).** When the exploded array is nested and the child rows need a parent key to stay joinable, `carry` copies named fields from the parent record onto every child (`{ dest_field: "source.dot.path" }`):

```yaml
- type: explode
  config: { path: values, prefix: "", carry: { employee_id: id } }
```

`{id: 7, values: [{v: a}, {v: b}]}` → `{v: a, employee_id: 7}`, `{v: b, employee_id: 7}`.

## `zip_columns` — columnar payload → one object per row (1→N)

Analytics / report APIs (e.g. Shopify ShopifyQL `tableData`) return results *positionally*: a list of column descriptors plus a list of value-arrays. `zip_columns` zips each row against the column names.

```yaml
- type: zip_columns
  config: { columns_path: "columns[*].name", rows_path: "rows" }
```

`{columns: [{name: day}, {name: sessions}], rows: [["2026-01-01", 12]]}` → `{day: "2026-01-01", sessions: 12}`. A row whose width differs from the column count fails loudly rather than misaligning fields. Gated on the `transform-zip-columns` feature (in `transforms` / `full`).

## Summary

Implements the twelve Meltano-migration connector/runtime gaps in one batch. Every stream that these gaps blocked can now be expressed config-only, and the tier-1 silent-data-loss bug in overwrite fan-out is fixed.

### Correctness (tier-1)

- **#552** `fix(executor,core)` — a matrix child (or product/discovery) fan-out over N parent records into a shared `write_mode: overwrite` sink used to truncate+swap the destination **once per invocation**, leaving only the last parent's rows (silent data loss on a green run). The executor now groups a level's overwrite invocations by their **resolved destination**, drives `begin_overwrite` once before the group and `commit_overwrite`/`abort_overwrite` once after (aborting if any invocation fails or the level is cancelled), and runs each invocation with the pipeline's overwrite lifecycle suppressed (`Pipeline::with_suppress_overwrite`). Per-parent destinations (`${parent.*}` in the table) stay single-member groups, unchanged. Verified by a core test + two SQLite end-to-end tests (all parents retained; a mid-run failure leaves the prior data intact).

### REST source (#547, #548, #549, #553, #554, #557)

- **#549** `record_ancestors` — lift enclosing envelope fields onto records unwrapped from a nested `records_path` (Stripe-events shape).
- **#547** `persist_cursor` — emit a `Cursor`/`CursorInBody` terminal cursor as the run bookmark and seed it into the next run's first request (Plaid `/transactions/sync` incremental resume).
- **#553** `OffsetInBody` pagination — offset/limit in the JSON request body (POST-query APIs).
- **#554** `RecordFieldCursor` pagination — keyset paging by the running max/min of a record field (Xero journals).
- **#557** `async_job` fetch **locator** — follow a result-set continuation (Salesforce Bulk `Sforce-Locator`-style header or a body field) across result pages.
- **#548** `records_multi` — emit several response arrays in one pass (one pagination advance), each stamped with a configurable `op_field`; pairs with a sink `write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` to route added/modified→upsert and removed→delete from one sync response. **Deliberately kept off the core `StreamPage` contract** — no core streaming-API change.

### Other connectors / transforms

- **#550** `feat(source-graphql)` — offset-into-query-variable pagination with short-page stop (ShopifyQL).
- **#551** `feat(core)` `zip_columns` transform — columnar `{columns, rows}` → one object per row (1→N; width mismatch errors loudly).
- **#555** `feat(transform)` `explode` gains `carry` — copy named parent fields onto each exploded child (kept CLI-side to avoid a `faucet-core` semver break on the frozen `ExplodeSpec`).
- **#556** `feat(auth)` `oauth2_refresh` — send `scope` on the refresh grant (rotated-refresh-token persistence was already shipped in #505; this completes the issue).
- **#558** reference table from a **live API** — an HTTP reference relation for the `transform-sql` transform (fetched once, cached for the run), which delivers the hibob id→label join the issue calls for.

## Testing / gates (verified locally, pinned toolchain)

- New tests: 3 (#552) · 6 REST wiremock + 50 REST unit · 15 graphql · 8 zip_columns/explode · auth + transform-sql suites. All green per crate.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo semver-checks -p faucet-core` — no update required (all faucet-core changes additive; the CI gate checks faucet-core only).
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps` — clean.
- Slim CLI build (`source-rest,sink-jsonl,sink-stdout,transforms`) — builds.
- `schemas/faucet.schema.json` regenerated (rest + graphql source defs; diff is surgical — `SinkConnector` and all other defs are byte-identical to `main`).

Docs: every touched crate README + the `pagination` and `transforms` cookbook pages updated.

How can I upgrade my homebrew's rust format?

Quick answer, then the caveat that matters for your CI situation. (I'm holding off on shell commands so I don't kill the background CI monitor — you can run these yourself, or type `! brew upgrade rust` in the prompt to run it in-session.)

## Upgrade Homebrew's rust (includes rustfmt)

```bash
brew update && brew upgrade rust
# verify:
rustfmt --version && brew info rust
```

## But this probably won't fix the CI mismatch

The `Format` failure wasn't because Homebrew's rustfmt was *old* — it was because it's a **different version than CI**, and rustfmt's line-wrapping is version-sensitive. CI pins the toolchain to **1.96.0** (`rustfmt 1.9.0-stable`). If you `brew upgrade rust` to the newest, its rustfmt could just as easily disagree with CI's 1.96.0 in the *other* direction. Chasing "latest Homebrew rustfmt" is the wrong target — you want "the **same** rustfmt CI uses."

The real fix is to let the rustup-pinned toolchain win locally, so `cargo fmt` uses the exact rustfmt CI does (it reads `rust-toolchain.toml` → 1.96.0):

**Option A — cleanest (remove the conflict):**
```bash
brew uninstall rust
```
You lose nothing — rustup already provides `cargo`/`rustc`/`rustfmt` via `~/.cargo/bin`, and they honor the repo's `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.96.0) automatically, matching CI. This is what your project's toolchain notes have flagged as the permanent fix.

**Option B — keep Homebrew rust, fix precedence:** put `~/.cargo/bin` ahead of `/opt/homebrew/bin` in your `~/.zshrc` `PATH`, and make sure rustfmt is in the pinned toolchain:
```bash
rustup component add rustfmt --toolchain 1.96.0
```

**Option C — per-invocation pin (no system change):**
```bash
RUSTFMT="$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/1.96.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustfmt" \
  "$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/1.96.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/cargo" fmt --all --check
```

My recommendation: **Option A** — uninstalling Homebrew rust ends this whole class of "local passes, CI fails" toolchain-shadowing bugs (it's bitten `rustc`, `rustdoc`, and now `rustfmt` on this machine). rustup then cleanly owns everything.

- **salesforce** — Bulk `fetch` had no continuation → added `Sforce-Locator` locator paging (#557); large objects no longer truncate.

- **stripe** — `subscription_history`/`discounts` now lift the envelope `event_id`/`event_created` via `record_ancestors` (#549), so that column is byte-faithful.

**Fixed 4 pre-existing template bugs** the now-stricter validate caught (the merged #444 compiles every row's transforms): acumatica (`explode` used `field:` not `path:`), oracle_fusion + ukg_pro (`${now}`/`${parent}` tokens in a `set` transform — unsupported), syteline (`cast` type `integer`→`int`, `on_error: keep`→`skip`).

- **hibob** — employee/entity faithful; the named-list id→label **columns** need the live-endpoint lookup (#558, shipped as a transform-sql HTTP relation — a template rewrite) + bulk-history explode-carry (#555).
- **syteline** — IDO entity streams fully config-driven; the report **stored-procedures** remain a caveat.
- **oracle_fusion** — the SOAP→XLSX report is faithful for **one period per run**; full history needs a per-period loop (`faucet backfill`).

- **sage** (blocked) — the Intacct `sessionid` is captured, but can't be injected into the raw XML request body every stream needs → filed **#567**. The one tap that doesn't deploy yet.

```

These come from hibob's company **named-lists** (`/v1/company/named-lists/<list>` — department / employment_type / title / work_change_type). Right now the template uses the `lookup` transform with `values: []` (empty placeholder), so those columns resolve to nothing.

**Why it's stuck on `lookup`:** the `lookup` transform can only read a reference table from **inline values or a local JSONL file** — it can't fetch from a live API. #558 (merged) added live-HTTP fetching, but to the **`transform-sql` reference relations** (a DuckDB `sql` transform), *not* to `lookup`. So to get live labels, each of the 5 lookups has to become a `sql` transform with an `http` relation.

3. **Basic auth on the reference fetch** — #558's http relation takes static `headers` only (not the shared `auth:` catalog), and hibob is HTTP Basic. **Lighter alternative (no DuckDB):** emit the named-lists as their own raw tables and do the id→label join in a downstream BigQuery/dbt model — the employee/work raw tables keep the raw id columns. Faithful to the *raw* layer and avoids the `sql`/DuckDB dependency entirely. This only differs from the tap if the tap's *raw* table must already contain the label column in-stream.

content.text:
Answering the API question now, then I'll set up the release watch.

## Template APIs (all bearer-auth on `/v1`, operator+ for writes)

**List / inspect registered templates:**
```bash
GET /v1/templates                 # list — latest version of every template
GET /v1/templates/{id}            # one template + its full state (versions, stable/previous/newest, launches)
GET /v1/templates/{id}?version=3  # a specific version (or ?version=stable|newest|prod|…)
```

**Run a registered template** — this is the one you asked for: **`POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs`** (handler `trigger_template`). It materializes the template (binds `params:`, drops the params block) and submits via the **same path as `POST /v1/runs`** — so idempotency, `doctor_first`, the queue, and cluster dispatch all apply. Request body:

```jsonc
{
  "params":  { "client_id":"…", "client_secret":"…", "refresh_token":"…",
               "tenant_id":"…", "bq_project":"my-proj", "bq_dataset":"raw", "sink":"bigquery" },
  "version": "stable",          // optional: a number or channel (stable/newest/prod/…); defaults to the launched version
  "env":     { "VAULT_ADDR":"…" }, // optional ${env:VAR} overrides for this run only
  "name":    "…",               // optional run-name override
  "labels":  { "team":"fin" },  // optional
  "doctor_first": true,         // optional preflight connectivity probe before running
  "idempotency_key": "xero-2026-08-24",  // optional replay-safe key
  "clock": "2026-08-24T00:00:00Z"        // optional ${now.*} override (e.g. backfill a date)
}
```

Concrete example:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/templates/xero-to-bigquery-or-jsonl/runs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"params":{"client_id":"…","client_secret":"…","refresh_token":"…","tenant_id":"…","bq_project":"my-proj","bq_dataset":"raw"},"doctor_first":true}'
```

**Response `202`:** the normal submit response **+** `template_id`, `template_version`, the (secret-redacted) bound `params`, and a `deprecated` note if the template is retired. Then track it exactly like any run:
```bash
GET  /v1/runs/{id}            # status
GET  /v1/runs/{id}/logs       # live SSE log stream
POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel     # cancel
```

So the full lifecycle per tap: `POST /v1/templates` (register, once) → `POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs` (run, per sync, with that tenant's params) → `GET /v1/runs/{id}`.

is there any ui option for it?

Yes — there's a full **web console** (the `serve-ui` feature), and preprod already has it: when I probed `/metrics` earlier it showed `/assets/{*path}` requests being served, which means the UI is compiled into your preprod build. So it's live at your port-forward.

**Open it:** `http://localhost:8080/` in a browser. The static shell is public; it prompts once for the **bearer token** (stored in `localStorage`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on every `/v1` call) — same token the API needs.

**Templates tab** gives you the whole lifecycle without curl:
- **Register** — a collapsible editor on the list page (paste the template YAML). Good for one-off/edits.
- **List** — every template with its status (draft / launched / deprecated) and stable / newest versions.
- **Per-template versions page** — assign channels (dev/test/staging/prod/canary), **Launch**, roll back, deprecate, delete, view the stored config, and the launch history.
- **Run** — a **typed trigger form auto-generated from the template's `params:` block**: it renders a field per param (client_id, refresh_token, bq_project, …, secrets masked), you fill them in and submit → it creates a run. Then the **Runs** view shows status + **live SSE logs**.

So you can register *and* run any tap straight from the browser.

**One practical note:** the UI is ideal for **triggering runs and managing versions**, but bulk-registering all **42** templates by pasting each YAML is tedious — for the initial bulk load the API (`POST /v1/templates`, which I'll drive) is faster. After that, the console is the nicer surface for day-to-day: pick a tap, fill the params form, run, watch logs.

(There's also a cookbook page — `docs/book/src/cookbook/web-console.md` — with screenshots of the Templates + versions views if you want the visual walkthrough.)

The release watcher is still running; I'll report the moment #538 merges → crates publish → the image + Helm chart are built.
ui option to run a template?

Yes. On the console, open a template (Templates tab → click the tap) → its **versions page** has a **typed "trigger/run" form auto-generated from that template's `params:` block**. Concretely:

1. `http://localhost:8080/` → **Templates** → click e.g. `xero-to-bigquery-or-jsonl`.
2. The page renders **one input per declared param** (client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, tenant_id, bq_project, bq_dataset, sink…), with **secrets masked**, defaults pre-filled, and a **version selector** (stable / a specific number / a channel).
3. Fill it in → **Run** → it submits (this is the UI calling `POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs` for you).
4. You're taken to the **Runs** view → live status + **SSE log stream**, with a cancel button.

So it's a point-and-click run per tap — pick the template, fill the params form, hit Run, watch logs. No curl needed. (It's operator+ / RunWrite, so it uses the same bearer token you enter once for the console.)

That said, it runs **one template at a time** via the form — there's no "run all 42" button in the UI. For fan-out/scheduling across many taps you'd script the API (`POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs`) or wire each into `faucet schedule` / an object-arrival trigger. But for on-demand "run this tap now," the console form is exactly it.

## Summary

faucet's config interpolation is **literal substitution only** (`${param.x}`, `${env:…}`, `${now.*}`, parent tokens). There's no way to **derive one value conditionally from another** — e.g. `accounts_domain = "zohocloud" if region == "ca" else "zoho"`. A value that is a pure function of another param must instead be surfaced as its own manually-set param with a default + a note, which is redundant and error-prone (a user can set an inconsistent pair).

## Motivation

Surfaced while building the Meltano-migration templates. `tap-zohobooks` exposes `accounts_domain` (default `zoho`; must be `zohocloud` only when `region=ca` → `accounts.zohocloud.ca`). It is **deterministically derivable from `region`**, but has to be its own param because the config can't express the conditional. Ties to template ergonomics / Third-Party Connector Friendliness: fewer redundant params ⇒ fewer misconfigurations. Any "value B keys off value A" case benefits (region→host segment, env→base URL, etc.).

## Proposed design

Add a small, **declarative, non-Turing-complete** derivation primitive to the interpolation layer — a map/lookup with a default, not an expression engine. Two candidate shapes (map is the simplest/safest):

- **Map-with-default token**, usable in source/sink configs:
  ```
  ${map:region|ca=zohocloud|*=zoho}
  ```
  Resolves the value of `region`, returns the matching case or the `*` default.

- **`computed` param** (preferred for the params surface):
  ```yaml
  params:
    region: { type: string, default: com }
    accounts_domain:
      type: string
      computed: "${map:region|ca=zohocloud|*=zoho}"   # derived, not user-supplied
  ```
  A `computed` param is **excluded from the trigger surface** (hidden from the console params form, `--param`, and the MCP/serve trigger body) and resolved **after** the ordinary params bind.

Resolution order: `${env:}`/`${file:}`/`${secret:}` → `${param.*}` bind → `computed`/`${map:}` → connector build.

## Affected crates / files

- `cli/src/interpolate.rs` — the `${map:…}` resolver + ordering.
- `cli/src/params/{spec,bind}.rs` — a `computed` field on the param spec; exclude computed params from the supplied/trigger surface; reject a supplied value for one.
- `cli/src/expand.rs` — `check_refs` accepts the new token; cycle detection over computed refs (reuse the existing `InterpolationCycle`).
- `docs/book/src/reference/config.md` (`## params` + interpolation), `faucet schema params`.

## Edge cases & failure modes

- **Cycles** (computed A → computed B → A) → detect + typed load-time error.
- A `computed` param must not be `required`/user-supplied — reject if a value is supplied for it.
- **Unmatched map key with no `*` default** → clear load-time error (never silently empty).
- Interaction with `secret: true` — a computed value is not a secret source; disallow or document.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tap-zohobooks` can drop the manual `accounts_domain` param: `region=ca` alone yields `accounts.zohocloud.ca`; any other region yields `accounts.zoho.<region>` — verified by a unit test over the interpolation.
- A `computed` param is hidden from the trigger/params form and rejected if a value is supplied for it.
- Cycles and unmatched-no-default surface as typed load-time errors.

## Out of scope

- A general expression language / arbitrary logic — keep it to map/lookup + default.
- Runtime (per-record) derivation — this is config-time only.

## References

Surfaced from the Meltano→faucet template migration (`tap-zohobooks` `accounts_domain`, derivable from `region`). Roadmap epic: #38.

Here's the answer, grounded in your actual redshift template.

## Where the BigQuery write credentials come from

Your `redshift-to-bigquery-or-jsonl.yaml` sink is:

```yaml
bigquery:
  type: bigquery
  config:
    project_id: "${param.bq_project}"
    dataset_id: "${param.bq_dataset}"
    table_id: "${param.table}"
    write_mode: overwrite
    auth: { type: application_default }
```

So the template supplies **only the *where*** — `bq_project`, `bq_dataset`, `table` (all params). It supplies **no credential at all**. `auth: { type: application_default }` tells the BigQuery sink to authenticate via **Google Application Default Credentials (ADC)** — resolved from the *runtime environment* of the `faucet serve` pod, not from the template, not from a param, not from a secret in the config.

The sink supports three auth types (`crates/common/bigquery/src/lib.rs`):

| `auth.type` | Credential source |
|---|---|
| `application_default` ← **what your template uses** | ADC chain (env / metadata server) |
| `service_account_key` | inline SA-key JSON in config (`config: { json: … }`) |
| `service_account_key_file` | path to an SA-key JSON on disk |

## The catch for your preprod cluster

ADC's resolution order is: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (a service-account key file) → gcloud user creds → **GCE/GKE metadata server** (the pod's attached GCP identity).

Your preprod runs on **AWS EKS**, which has **no GCP metadata server**. So `application_default` there resolves *only* if one of these is true:

1. **A GCP service-account key JSON is mounted into the pod** and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` points at it (the simplest, deployment-level fix — applies to every tap at once, no per-template change), **or**
2. **GCP Workload Identity Federation** is configured (EKS OIDC → GCP), so the pod's AWS identity is federated to a GCP SA with no key file.

If neither is set up, a redshift→BigQuery run will start fine (redshift source connects on its own DB params) and then **fail at the first BigQuery write** with an ADC-not-found error — the source creds and sink creds are completely independent.

python3 - <<'PY'
import re, glob, sys

OLD_AUTH = "auth: { type: application_default }"
NEW_AUTH = 'auth: { type: service_account_key, config: { json: "${param.bq_sa_key}" } }'

# matches a bq_dataset param DECLARATION line, capturing indent + spacing before '{'
DATASET_RE = re.compile(r'^(?P<indent>\s*)bq_dataset:(?P<sp>\s*)\{[^\n]*\}\s*$')

changed, skipped = [], []
for path in sorted(glob.glob("*.yaml")):
    src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    problems = []

    # 1) auth swap
    n_auth = src.count(OLD_AUTH)
    if n_auth != 1:
        problems.append(f"expected 1 application_default, found {n_auth}")
    src2 = src.replace(OLD_AUTH, NEW_AUTH)

    # 2) insert bq_sa_key param after the bq_dataset declaration
    lines = src2.splitlines(keepends=True)
    out, inserted = [], 0
    for ln in lines:
        out.append(ln)
        m = DATASET_RE.match(ln)
        if m:
            indent, sp = m.group("indent"), m.group("sp")
            # keep '{' aligned: bq_sa_key is 1 char shorter than bq_dataset
            newsp = sp + " "
            nl = "\n" if ln.endswith("\n") else "\n"
            out.append(f'{indent}bq_sa_key:{newsp}{{ type: string, default: "", secret: true, description: "BigQuery service-account key JSON (inline); required when sink=bigquery" }}{nl}')
            inserted += 1
    if inserted != 1:
        problems.append(f"expected 1 bq_dataset decl, inserted {inserted}")
    src3 = "".join(out)

    if problems:
        skipped.append((path, "; ".join(problems)))
        continue
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src3)
    changed.append(path)

print(f"CHANGED {len(changed)} files")
if skipped:
    print("SKIPPED (needs manual review):")
    for p, why in skipped:
        print(f"  {p}: {why}")
PY

Design choices:
- **`secret: true`** → the value is registered with the redaction boundary, so it never appears in logs/traces/error output.
- **`default: ""`** (not `required`) → a `sink=jsonl` run still works without supplying it (the bigquery sink block isn't materialized in that case). For a `sink=bigquery` run you pass the JSON; if you forget, the sink fails cleanly at build ("invalid service-account key"), never silently.

or `--param-env bq_sa_key` pointing at an env var holding the JSON (avoids escaping on the CLI), or in the console's typed trigger form (it renders `bq_sa_key` as a secret field).

content.text:
Done. All 42 preprod templates now use the inline service-account-key mechanism, live and launched.

## Result

- **47 local templates** edited: BigQuery sink auth swapped from `application_default` → `service_account_key` with `config: { json: "${param.bq_sa_key}" }`, plus a new `bq_sa_key` secret param.
- **46/47 validate** locally (only `sage` fails, on its pre-existing `${session_id}` blocker #567 — unrelated to this change).
- **42 preprod templates re-registered as v2 and launched** (`http://localhost:8080`, earlier bearer token). Verified all 42 carry `bq_sa_key` (secret) and are stable at v2.

## How runs now get BigQuery credentials

At trigger time you supply the full SA-key JSON as one param value:

```json
POST /v1/templates/redshift-to-bigquery-or-jsonl/runs
{ "params": {
    "sink": "bigquery",
    "bq_project": "…", "bq_dataset": "…",
    "bq_sa_key": "{\"type\":\"service_account\",\"project_id\":\"…\", … }"
} }
```

- It's `secret: true`, so it's redacted from logs/traces/errors.
- `default: ""` keeps `sink=jsonl` runs working without it; a `sink=bigquery` run that omits it fails cleanly at sink build, not silently.
- The pod no longer needs any GCP identity/ADC — each run brings its own key.

## Two things to note

1. The **5 non-registered templates** (`ukg_pro`, `syteline`, `oracle_fusion` = CORE; `shopify` = partial #569; `sage` = blocked #567) also got the edit locally but weren't on preprod, so nothing to re-register there.
2. **Rotate the pasted bearer token** if it's long-lived — it's now in this transcript.

Old v1 (ADC) still exists on each template as history; a `rollback`/`launch v1` would revert if ever needed.

content.text:
Confirmed from the sink code. Short answer: **no — nothing is auto-created, and for your templates the table must exist too.**

## What actually happens

**The dataset is never created.** There's no `create_dataset` / `CREATE SCHEMA` anywhere in the BigQuery sink. If `bq_dataset` doesn't exist, the first BigQuery call returns a **404 and the run fails cleanly** — no silent success, no partial write.

**Your templates all use `write_mode: overwrite`, which also requires the *target table* to pre-exist.** The overwrite lifecycle's first step is (`crates/sink/bigquery/src/sink.rs:908`):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE <dataset>.<table>__faucet_ovw LIKE <dataset>.<table>
```

`... LIKE <target>` needs the target table to already exist (that's how it copies the schema + partitioning/clustering). If the table is missing, `begin_overwrite` fails with `Not found: Table …` before any data is written. The code comment says it outright: *"The target must already exist (LIKE requires it) — overwrite replaces its rows, not its schema."*

Even in plain append mode it wouldn't help you here — `tabledata.insertAll` doesn't create tables either, and the sink has no create-table path for the data table.

## Practical implication for the fleet

Before triggering any `sink=bigquery` run, the destination must be pre-provisioned:

1. **The dataset** (`bq_dataset`) must exist in `bq_project`.
2. **Every target table** must exist with the correct schema. Remember these are multi-stream matrix templates — each row writes its own `table_id` (e.g. bamboohr → `employment`, `payroll`, `work`, `employee`, `job_titles`, …). *All* of those tables must be pre-created, not just one.

A `sink=jsonl` run has none of this requirement (it just writes files).

## If you'd rather it auto-create

That's a real gap for a migration workflow — pre-creating dozens of tables per tap by hand is painful. Two ways forward, if you want:
- Add an opt-in `auto_create: true` to the BigQuery sink (create dataset + infer/create table from the first page's schema when absent) — I can file this as an enhancement and implement it.
- Or keep provisioning external (Terraform / a one-time `bq mk` script) and leave the sink strict.

## Important — datasets exist, tables still don't

Creating the dataset clears only *half* the pre-provisioning requirement. Remember from the sink behavior:

- **`write_mode: overwrite` (what all templates use) requires each target *table* to already exist** — `begin_overwrite` runs `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE …__faucet_ovw LIKE <target>`, which fails with `Not found: Table` if the target table is missing.
- Each template is multi-stream: every matrix row writes its own `table_id` (bamboohr → `employment`, `payroll`, `work`, `employee`, `job_titles`, …). **All of those tables need to exist**, with the right schema, before a `sink=bigquery` run will succeed.

So a run against a fresh `tenant2425_*` dataset will still fail at the first overwrite until the tables are created.

Two ways to close that gap — want me to do either?

1. **Implement `auto_create` on the BigQuery sink** (create the table from the first page's inferred schema when it's absent; and optionally auto-create the dataset too). This is the durable fix — I'd file it as an enhancement, implement, test, ship, then re-register the templates. It removes the manual table step entirely.
2. **Pre-create the tables now** — but that needs a known schema per stream. Without a schema source I'd have to either run each tap once to JSONL and infer, or you supply DDL. Messier and per-tap.

My recommendation is **option 1** — it's the right long-term behavior for a migration tool and fixes all 47 at once. Should I proceed with it?

Also: point the templates' `bq_project`/`bq_dataset` params at these — trigger with `bq_project=drivetrain-preprod` and `bq_dataset=tenant2425_<tap>`.

| `table_id` | string | — *(required)* | BigQuery table ID. Created automatically on first write when missing (see [Table creation](#table-creation)); set `create_table: false` to require it to pre-exist. |
| `auth` | `BigQueryCredentials` | — *(required)* | Authentication — see [Authentication](#authentication). |

### Table creation

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `create_table` | bool | `true` | Create the target table (and its dataset) if it does not exist, inferring the schema from the first written page — a first-ever sync cannot assume the table exists. Set to `false` to require the table to pre-exist and fail fast when it is missing (e.g. the schema is managed externally and a missing table signals a typo). |
| `location` | string | *(unset)* | Dataset location (region or multi-region, e.g. `US`, `EU`, `us-central1`) used only when `create_table` has to create the dataset. Unset uses the BigQuery job's default location; ignored once the dataset exists. |

When `create_table` is on and the table is missing, the schema is inferred from the first page: JSON scalars map to `INT64` / `FLOAT64` / `BOOL` / `STRING`, and nested objects/arrays to `JSON`. For `write_mode: overwrite`, the target and its staging clone are created on the first page (before the atomic swap); for `append`/`upsert`/`delete` the table is created before the first write. An empty source produces no schema, so nothing is created — the run is a clean no-op. If later pages introduce new columns, pair with a [`schema:` drift policy](../../../docs/book/src/cookbook/schema-drift.md) set to `evolve`.

While the push runs, let me give the user an interim update on where things stand and the immediate unblock, since they're actively hitting this on preprod.

The root cause of your latest error is different from the 404: the table `cohort_ggr_ngr` now **exists but has no schema** (created by a bare `bq mk` with no `--schema`), so BigQuery's `CREATE … LIKE` rejects it. The deployed preprod build (v1.11.0) can't fix that on its own.

What I've built handles **both** cases — a missing table *and* a schemaless one:

- Readiness is now decided by "does the target have a usable schema (≥1 field)?" — a missing table (404) and a schemaless table both count as "not ready".
- When not ready and `create_table` is on (the default), the sink runs `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … (<inferred columns>)` from the first page, which **replaces the schemaless table** with a real schema (a table that already has a schema is used as-is and never dropped).
- Works across append, upsert/delete, exactly-once, and overwrite (overwrite creates the target + staging on the first page, then swaps).

The feature is committed with unit + wiremock tests all green. I'm pushing it now and will open the PR + arm auto-merge.

**Two immediate options for preprod while this ships:**
1. **Fastest right now, no new build:** drop the schemaless placeholder tables so they're simply absent — but the currently-deployed v1.11.0 will then 404 again (it has neither fix). So this only helps *after* the new build deploys.
2. **The real fix:** merge this → release → redeploy the chart. Then a run against an empty *or* schemaless `tenant2425_*` table just works.

So the sequence is: land this PR → cut a release → you redeploy the chart → re-run. I'll drive the PR/merge and report when it's merged and released.

Verified the run model. Here's the accurate picture (and it matters for your preprod, which `/readyz` reports as **non-clustered**).

## 1. Is there a "rerun" option today?

**No.** The run endpoints are only:
```
POST /v1/runs            (create)
GET  /v1/runs, /v1/runs/{id}
DELETE /v1/runs/{id}
POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel
GET  /v1/runs/{id}/logs
```
There is no `POST /v1/runs/{id}/rerun`. "Rerunning" today means **re-submitting** — for a template, calling `POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs` again with the same params; for a raw config, re-POSTing the body. If you pass the **same `idempotency_key`**, the server replays (returns the existing run) instead of duplicating — that's the replay-safety mechanism, not a rerun.

## 2. Does a run store the values passed to it?

**On your preprod (non-clustered): no — not the inputs.** A `RunRecord` stores: `name`, `labels`, `status`, timings, `records_written`, `error`, `idempotency_key`, a `doctor_report`, and a **config fingerprint** (sha256). The full config and the param values are **not** persisted:

- `config_body` is explicitly *"present only for cluster runs so any instance can re-resolve + re-run it. `None` for single-instance runs."*
- There is no `params`/`env` field on the record at all.
- **Secret params (`bq_sa_key`) are never stored anywhere** — by design. Even in cluster mode, a template trigger *refuses* caller-supplied `secret: true` params precisely so they don't land in the shared history DB.

So the stored run alone can't reconstruct itself: template runs keep `template` + `template_version` labels (so you know *what* ran), but not the `bq_project` / `bq_dataset` / `bq_sa_key` values used.

## What this means for your workflow

To re-run a template you must re-supply the params, including the secret `bq_sa_key`, every time. That's the friction you're sensing.

**My recommendation (decisive):** move the SA key out of a trigger param and into a **server-side reference** in the template body — `auth: { type: service_account_key, config: { json: "${vault:…}" } }` or `${env:GCP_SA_KEY}`. Then:
- Reruns need **no secret input** — the server resolves it at run time from Vault/env.
- Nothing secret ever touches the trigger call, the run record, or (in cluster mode) the history DB.
- Only the non-secret params (`bq_project`, `bq_dataset`, `sink`) are passed per run, and those are safe to remember.

That directly gives you "rerun without re-typing the key" and is strictly more secure than storing values.

If you also want a literal **rerun button/endpoint**, I'd build it as: persist the *non-secret* params on the run record (or per-template "last inputs"), add `POST /v1/runs/{id}/rerun` + a console button that re-triggers the same template+version with those remembered params, and require any `secret: true` inputs to be re-supplied (or, better, sourced from `${vault:}` as above so nothing is required). That's a clean, separately-shippable feature.

Want me to (a) file that rerun feature as an issue (and implement after the current PR lands), (b) switch the templates' `bq_sa_key` to a `${vault:}`/`${env:}` server-side reference now, or both? Meanwhile the auto-create PR is mid-push — I'll land it regardless.

**No — and please don't run it against that table.** Adding one random column gets you past the "does not have a schema" error, but it will then **silently drop all your real data**.

Here's why (just confirmed in the sink code): the BigQuery overwrite path shapes its `INSERT` to the **target table's** columns, not the incoming data's. `build_insert_select` builds the column list and the `SELECT … FROM UNNEST(@payload)` **only from `target_schema()`** — any field in your records that isn't a column of the target table is never selected. So with a target that has just your one random column:

- The insert writes **only that one column**; every actual Redshift column is dropped.
- That column probably doesn't exist in the source rows, so it lands as **all NULL** — or the run errors if you made it `NOT NULL`.

Either way the result is wrong. Getting past the error message here is worse than the error, because it's **silent data loss** — the run goes green while the destination ends up with one column of nulls.

Two things to know:

1. **On the currently deployed build (v1.11.0):** the sink never adapts the table to the data. It only ever writes the columns the table already has. So the *only* way it works correctly today is if the table already exists with the **full, correct schema** (all the columns your Redshift query produces).

2. **Even after my auto-create fix deploys, the random column defeats it.** My fix only creates/replaces a table that is *missing* or *has zero columns*. A table that already has a schema — even a wrong one-column schema — is treated as "ready" and used as-is → same data loss. So a partial placeholder is the one thing you must not leave in place.

What to do instead:

- **Simplest correct path:** `bq rm -f -t drivetrain-preprod:tenant2425_redshift.cohort_ggr_ngr` to drop it entirely, then run **after the auto-create build is deployed** — it will infer the full schema from the first page. (On v1.11.0 a dropped table just 404s, so this needs the new build.)
- **Works on any build:** pre-create the table with the **complete** schema (every column the query returns), e.g. `bq mk --schema field1:TYPE,field2:TYPE,… -t …cohort_ggr_ngr`. Then overwrite writes all columns correctly.
- **Do not** pre-create with a partial/placeholder schema.

So the real unblock is landing + deploying the auto-create PR (in flight), then dropping any placeholder tables so it can build the right schema from the data. Want me to prioritize getting that build released and walk you through the redeploy?

=================== #567 ===================
TITLE: feat(auth,source): inject a flow-captured value into a raw request body (XML/text)
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: ['enhancement', 'tier-2']

## Summary
The `flow` auth provider can `capture` a value (e.g. a session id from an XML login response) and `apply` it to a **placement** (header/query/cookie/JSON-body-field), but it cannot substitute it into a **raw request body string** — which is what an XML gateway needs (`<sessionid>${session_id}</sessionid>`). The CLI interpolation pass also rejects `${session_id}` outright (unknown id), so a source `body:` cannot reference a captured value.

## Motivation
`tap-sage` (Intacct XML gateway): every data request's XML body must carry the `sessionid` captured from the `getAPISession` login. With no way to place a captured value into the raw XML body, the sage template cannot authenticate — it's the one tap of 47 that does not validate.

## Proposed design
Let the flow provider's `apply` (or the source) substitute `${<capture_name>}` tokens in the request **body string** (and headers) at request time, and teach the CLI interpolation to treat flow-capture names as deferred tokens (like `${parent.*}`) rather than rejecting them.

## Affected
`crates/auth/src/flow.rs` (apply → body-string substitution), `crates/source/xml` + `crates/source/rest` (body token substitution from the resolved auth context), `cli/src/interpolate.rs` / `expand.rs` (don't reject flow-capture tokens).

## Acceptance
A flow provider captures a value and a source's raw XML/text `body:` references it via `${name}`, substituted per request. Roadmap: #38

=================== #568 ===================
TITLE: feat(transform): set/stamp a column from a runtime token (parent record / ${now.*})
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: ['enhancement', 'tier-2']

## Summary
The `set` transform stamps a **constant**; it cannot take a value from a runtime token — a parent-record reference (`${company.company_id}`) or a clock token (`${now.*}`). Those resolve only in source/sink configs, so stamping a parent/derived id **as a column** isn't expressible.

## Motivation
- `tap-ukg_pro` `user_defined_field` (child of `company`): needs the parent `company_id` as a disambiguation column — `set { company_id: ${company.company_id} }` fails.
- `tap-oracle_fusion`: the report `period` column wants `${now.strftime.%b-%y}`; a `${now.*}` param default can't feed a `set`.

Distinct from #555 (explode carry): this is a non-explode per-row stamp of a runtime value.

## Proposed design
Allow `${parent.*}` and `${now.*}` tokens in the `set` transform's values, resolved per record against the same fan-out/clock context the source/sink configs use.

## Affected
`cli/src/transforms.rs` (set decode/compile), `cli/src/executor.rs` (thread the row's parent/now context into the set stage), `faucet-core` `RecordTransform::Set` (accept a resolved value map).

## Acceptance
A child row stamps its parent key as a column via `set`; a `${now.*}` set value resolves per run. Roadmap: #38

=================== #569 ===================
TITLE: feat(source-graphql): offset-into-query-STRING substitution for ShopifyQL (#550 follow-up)
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: ['enhancement', 'tier-2']

## Summary
#550 added graphql `Offset` pagination by injecting the offset as a GraphQL **variable** (`variables.{offset_variable} = <n>`). But **ShopifyQL** embeds `LIMIT/OFFSET` **inside the query string** (`shopifyqlQuery(query: "... LIMIT 250 OFFSET <n>")`) — a GraphQL variable cannot interpolate into a string-literal argument, so #550 as merged does **not** actually page ShopifyQL.

## Motivation
`tap-shopify` `sessions` + `sales` use ShopifyQL. They remain the only non-config-driven shopify streams (orders/customers/products page fine via Relay cursors). Verified against the merged #550 code: `map.insert(off.offset_variable, json!(offset))` — variable injection, not string substitution.

## Proposed design
Add a string-substitution mode to the graphql Offset paginator: substitute `${offset_variable}` occurrences in the query string (and/or a named GraphQL variable's string value) with the current offset before each request. Pair with `zip_columns` (#551) for the columnar `tableData`.

## Affected
`crates/source/graphql/src/stream.rs` (offset string substitution alongside variable injection), `config.rs` (a `substitute_in_query` flag).

## Acceptance
A ShopifyQL query pages by an offset substituted into the query string and stops on a short page (wiremock). Roadmap: #38

=================== #573 ===================
TITLE: feat(cli): map/conditional interpolation to derive one config value from another (computed params)
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: ['enhancement', 'tier-3']

## Summary

faucet's config interpolation is **literal substitution only** (`${param.x}`, `${env:…}`, `${now.*}`, parent tokens). There's no way to **derive one value conditionally from another** — e.g. `accounts_domain = "zohocloud" if region == "ca" else "zoho"`. A value that is a pure function of another param must instead be surfaced as its own manually-set param with a default + a note, which is redundant and error-prone (a user can set an inconsistent pair).

## Motivation

Surfaced while building the Meltano-migration templates. `tap-zohobooks` exposes `accounts_domain` (default `zoho`; must be `zohocloud` only when `region=ca` → `accounts.zohocloud.ca`). It is **deterministically derivable from `region`**, but has to be its own param because the config can't express the conditional. Ties to template ergonomics / Third-Party Connector Friendliness: fewer redundant params ⇒ fewer misconfigurations. Any "value B keys off value A" case benefits (region→host segment, env→base URL, etc.).

## Proposed design

Add a small, **declarative, non-Turing-complete** derivation primitive to the interpolation layer — a map/lookup with a default, not an expression engine. Two candidate shapes (map is the simplest/safest):

- **Map-with-default token**, usable in source/sink configs:
  ```
  ${map:region|ca=zohocloud|*=zoho}
  ```
  Resolves the value of `region`, returns the matching case or the `*` default.

- **`computed` param** (preferred for the params surface):
  ```yaml
  params:
    region: { type: string, default: com }
    accounts_domain:
      type: string
      computed: "${map:region|ca=zohocloud|*=zoho}"   # derived, not user-supplied
  ```
  A `computed` param is **excluded from the trigger surface** (hidden from the console params form, `--param`, and the MCP/serve trigger body) and resolved **after** the ordinary params bind.

Resolution order: `${env:}`/`${file:}`/`${secret:}` → `${param.*}` bind → `computed`/`${map:}` → connector build.

## Affected crates / files

- `cli/src/interpolate.rs` — the `${map:…}` resolver + ordering.
- `cli/src/params/{spec,bind}.rs` — a `computed` field on the param spec; exclude computed params from the supplied/trigger surface; reject a supplied value for one.
- `cli/src/expand.rs` — `check_refs` accepts the new token; cycle detection over computed refs (reuse the existing `InterpolationCycle`).
- `docs/book/src/reference/config.md` (`## params` + interpolation), `faucet schema params`.

## Edge cases & failure modes

- **Cycles** (computed A → computed B → A) → detect + typed load-time error.
- A `computed` par

68	/// Offset-into-query-variable pagination (ShopifyQL and similar).
69	///
70	/// Increments an integer offset injected into a GraphQL variable and
71	/// terminates on a **short page** (fewer than `page_size` records) — unlike
72	/// cursor pagination, which follows a `pageInfo` boolean. Suited to APIs whose
73	/// query language embeds `LIMIT … OFFSET …` (e.g. ShopifyQL): bake the limit
74	/// into the query string and parameterize only the offset with `${…}`.
75	///
76	/// The offset starts at `0`, is sent as a JSON number in the `variables` map on
77	/// every request, and advances by `page_size` after each page.
78	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
79	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
80	pub struct GraphqlOffsetPagination {
81	    /// Discriminator — must be `Offset`.
82	    pub r#type: OffsetPaginationKind,
83	    /// Name of the GraphQL variable that receives the current offset. It is
84	    /// injected as a JSON number (starting at `0`, incremented by `page_size`
85	    /// after each page). Reference it from the query string or as a variable
86	    /// (e.g. `${q_offset}` for ShopifyQL).
87	    pub offset_variable: String,
