echo "=== any overflow/transform/contain on .page/.view ==="; grep -nE "transform|contain|will-change|overflow|filter|perspective" cli/src/serve/ui/styles.css | grep -iE "page|view|animation|rise"

content.text:
**Found the root cause.** `.page` has `animation: rise` that animates `transform` with `fill-mode: both` — and in Chrome, an element with a filling `transform` animation is a **containing block** even when the current transform is `none`. So the sticky `<thead>` was sticking to `.page` (which scrolls away) instead of the viewport. That's the whole bug. The standard fix: don't animate `transform` on the ancestor, and pin the header just below the (working) sticky nav.

## Live UI verification (serve web console / `serve-ui`)

**Frontend quality is entirely yours to own — detecting and fixing UI bugs is your job, never the user's.** The user's time is for platform-level, architectural, and product decisions, not for pointing out that a button is misaligned, a dropdown doesn't close, dark mode is broken, text is wrapping, or a header isn't sticky. Treat every one of those as a defect you must find and fix *before* handing work back. Assume the role of an expert frontend/UI engineer, not a junior who ships and waits for review. **After any UI change — and before saying "done" — run the full live sweep yourself (below), in both themes, clicking every interactive element, and fix everything you find.** If the user ever has to report a visual bug, that is a process failure on your side: you skipped the render pass. Do not make them do it twice.

**For any non-trivial change to the web console (`cli/src/serve/ui/**` — JS/CSS/HTML), verify it in a real rendered browser, not just by reading the code.**

content.text: The DOM is simple — `.topbar` and `.view` are both direct children of `<body>`, so `position: sticky; top:0` should hold the whole way. Something on `html`/`body` is confining it. Let me check:

content.text: **Found the root cause.** Line 123: `html, body { height: 100%; }` — this caps `<body>` at exactly one viewport height (813px), but the content is ~3336px and overflows. Since `.topbar`'s `position: sticky` containing block is `<body>`, it can only stick **within `<body>`'s 813px box** — so once you scroll past one screen, the body's box scrolls above the viewport and the topbar goes with it. That's the "nav disappears after scrolling" bug exactly. The fix is `min-height` instead of `height`:

cat > "$SCRATCH/issue_discovery.md" <<'MD'
## Summary

A multi-object source (Salesforce, and by extension any catalog/describe-backed API or DB) currently requires **one hand-written matrix row per object**, each carrying an explicit column list (`SELECT <fields> FROM <Object>`) and a destination `table_id`. Let operators **declare the sync once** and have faucet **enumerate the objects — and their fields — from the source's own describe/catalog API**, generating the per-object syncs automatically.

Concretely, the Salesforce template (`drivetrain/templates/salesforce-to-bigquery-or-jsonl.yaml`) defines the connection, OAuth, Bulk-API 2.0 job shape, and sink **once** (the `default` template), then hand-lists `account` / `contact` / `lead` / `opportunity` / … as matrix rows, each repeating a bespoke SOQL field list. That per-object enumeration is the part that shouldn't be manual.

## Motivation

- **Reliability (Primary Goal):** hand-maintained object + field lists drift from the org schema — a new SObject or a new field is **silently missed** until someone edits YAML. Describe-driven generation makes coverage track the source.
- **Operator ergonomics / third-party friendliness:** a 50-object org means 50 rows × bespoke field lists to write and maintain. "Define the connection once + a selection filter" is the expected shape.
- Salesforce already exposes everything needed: `/services/data/vXX/sobjects` (global describe) → object list; per-object describe → queryable field list.

## Proposed design

Two complementary layers (either is useful alone; together they're the full story):

1. **`faucet discover` for the REST/Bulk source (extends #211).** A discovery hook that hits global describe → objects, per-object describe → field list, applies `--include`/`--exclude` globs + a configurable blacklist, and emits one `DatasetDescriptor` per object whose `config_patch` carries the generated SOQL + `table_id`. `faucet discover` then materializes the matrix. This is generation-time (explicit, reviewable output).

2. **Config-level dynamic fan-out (`for_each` / discovery-source).** A matrix template that runs **once per item returned by a "list" step**, so fan-out happens at *run* time and new objects are picked up without a config edit. Reuse the existing parent/child matrix machinery (`parent:` rows + `${parent.path}` tokens, `cli/src/expand.rs`); the missing pieces are (a) a describe→field-list resolver and (b) `SELECT *`-style field expansion token.

Config sketch (layer 2):

```yaml
matrix:
  - id: objects            # parent: enumerate sobjects (global describe)
    source: { ref: default, config: { ...describe list... } }
  - id: sync
    parent: objects
    source: { ref: default, config: { async_job: { submit: { json: {
      query: "SELECT ${objects.fields} FROM ${objects.name}" } } } } }
    sink: { ref: "${param.sink}", config: { table_id: "${objects.name_snake}" } }
```

`${objects.fields}` expands to the queryable field list (excluding compound/unsupported types), with an optional per-object override map for the rare object that needs curation.

## Affected crates / files

- `crates/source/rest/` — describe/discovery hook + field-list resolver (no new connector; standing preference is no new source crates).
- `crates/core/src/discover.rs` — `DatasetDescriptor` already exists; add field-list + SOQL helpers.
- `cli/src/commands/discover.rs` — Salesforce/REST branch + generated-matrix emission.
- `cli/src/expand.rs` — dynamic (`parent:`-driven) fan-out + `${…​.fields}` token.
- `faucet-local-demo/drivetrain/templates/salesforce-to-bigquery-or-jsonl.yaml` — migrate to the fan-out shape (and remove the stale `TODO(#531)` — #531 was HubSpot-specific and is closed).

## Edge cases & failure modes

- Objects with no queryable fields; compound / geolocation / base64 / address fields (exclude from `SELECT`).
- SOQL length limit for very wide objects (chunk or fall back to a curated list).
- Custom `__c` objects; `queryAll` vs `query` (deleted rows); describe **rate limits** (cache the describe result per run).
- An object that disappears between describe and query (skip + warn, don't fail the whole run).
- Determinism: the generated matrix must be stable-ordered so state keys / lineage don't churn.

## Acceptance criteria

- `faucet discover` against a Salesforce config generates a matrix covering all non-blacklisted objects with correct, type-filtered field lists.
- (Layer 2) a run picks up a newly-created object without a config edit.
- Field lists exclude unsupported types; per-object override honored.
- Existing hand-written templates keep working (opt-in).

## Out of scope

- Non-Salesforce describe dialects in v1 (design the token/hook generically; implement Salesforce first).
- Column-level lineage derived from describe.

## References

- #211 (`faucet discover` — live catalog introspection, the pattern to extend)
- #531 (closed — HubSpot chained/two-level discovery; prior art, and the stale ref in the current template)
- `drivetrain/templates/salesforce-to-bigquery-or-jsonl.yaml`
- Roadmap epic #38

  --body-file "$SCRATCH/issue_discovery.md" 2>&1 | tail -1)

content.text:
All shipped and filed. Here's where everything landed:

## The sticky-header bug — root-caused and actually fixed
I stopped guessing and measured it. The nav's `position: sticky` was breaking because of **`html, body { height: 100% }`** — that caps `<body>`'s box at exactly one viewport, and a sticky element can only stick *within its parent's box*. So once the page grew past one screen, `<body>`'s box scrolled above the viewport and the nav went with it, leaving the still-pinned table header with rows visible in the gap above it. Every "row above the header" report traces to this one line. Fix: `body { min-height: 100% }`. Verified via headless at scrollY 800 / 1200 / 2483 — nav stays pinned, no rows in the gap. My earlier top-offset/z-index/keyframe tweaks were treating symptoms; this is the root. **(pushed)**

## Lineage — done as you described
Click a dataset → it goes solid teal, its connected datasets get a teal tint, the linking edges light up, everything else dims; click again or the background to clear; double-click opens it. Labels now show the full path (capped, then the graph **scrolls left/right** — the SVG keeps its natural width instead of squashing to fit). Verified light + dark. **(pushed)**

## "Load more" — now a centered pill instead of a stray ghost box. **(pushed)**

Fixed and pushed (`39ee478c`). 

The real bug: my `.load-more { display: block }` rule (added for centering) outranked the browser's built-in `[hidden] { display: none }` — same specificity, and author styles win over user-agent styles — so setting `hidden = true` had no visible effect. The button stayed on screen at the end of the list. And my earlier "verified" was hollow because I checked the `.hidden` *property* (which was correctly `true`) instead of the rendered `display`.

Added `.load-more[hidden] { display: none }` so the hidden attribute wins, and this time verified against the **computed display**: `block` while there's a next page → `none` the moment the last page loads. So the button now genuinely disappears once you reach the end. Reload 18080 to pick it up.
